subject: Capacity runway & latency playbook — follow-up from discovery
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@averytech.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@averytech.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + priorities from today

Laura / Redwood team —

Thanks for carving time today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can keep momentum: 

Pain points we emphasised:
- Production latency spikes impacting interactive search (p95 bursts up to ~800ms during peak).
- High per-token cost driving down volume for features that need short responses (10-40 tokens).
- Ops overhead: our current on-prem infra is single-region; need a predictable scaling model and auditability for SOC2.

Goals we set:
- Serve interactive search at p95 <= 150ms (target for 32-token completions).
- Reduce per-request cost by ~30% relative to our current managed endpoint through batching/caching/quantization.
- Have a 3-month runway plan for scaling from 50k to 250k monthly queries with predictable capacity commitments.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you share a recommended topology + cost/latency tradeoffs for: hosted vs dedicated vs private?
2) Example latency profile for a model family that balances quality vs cost (we're looking at open 70B-family models).
3) Any security checklist items for Private deployment (KMS/HSM, VPC peering) we should budget for.

We're copying Samantha (engineering lead) to align on technical owners. Would love a short write-up we can share with finance/by EOD Monday.

Cheers,
Jordan
Sr. Product Manager — AveryTech

--

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + priorities from today

Jordan — great to meet today. Short post-call recap and a proposed action plan below. Attaching a starter capacity runway spreadsheet and sample latency profiles to make the numbers concrete.

Recap (short):
- Primary user flow: interactive search (median prompt length ~12 tokens, response length ~28 tokens).
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 150ms for 32-token responses; p50 near 40–60ms.
- Traffic shape: current baseline ~50 QPS with daily peaks up to 120 QPS; expected to scale to sustained 300 QPS within 3 months if conversion goes well.
- Security: SOC2 evidence and KMS integration are must-haves for procurement.

Action plan & owners:
- Laura: deliver concise topology + hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs (this thread) — deliverable: summary + deployment sketch (attached).
- Karthik: deep-dive on model choices, quantization, and batching knobs; include p95 latency estimates on p4/p5 style GPUs — ETA: Monday EOD.
- Vivek: cost estimate and potential reserved capacity plan for Dedicated — ETA: Tue COB unless you need earlier.

Initial recommendations (high level):
- Short-term: Hosted API with prefix caching + dynamic batching for immediate time-to-value. Configure KV cache for recent prefixes (TTL 30m) to reduce per-token compute on common queries.
- Medium-term: Move to Dedicated pool pinned to a quantized 70B variant (INT8/4-bit as applicable) for predictable latency and cost. Reserve a small burst pool in hosted to handle unexpected spikes.
- Private (if required for procurement): Recommend VPC deployment behind customer-controlled ingress and a KMS-managed key for model keys/audit logs. Allow for a cross-region read replica for DR.

See attached: avt_capacity_runway_v1.xlsx and latency_profile_samples.csv for numbers used below.

Next steps: we’ll send a technical sketch + rough cost delta by Tue. Can we tentatively book a 45-min deep dive with Karthik and your infra lead on Tue (9/15) or Wed (9/16)?

Best,
Laura Bennett

From: karthik.iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@averytech.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Technical deep-dive: latency-throughput sketch + model tradeoffs

Jordan / Laura / Samantha —

Following our notes, here are concrete technical sketches and engineering tradeoffs to consider. I focused on worst-case p95 and predictable throughput for interactive workloads.

1) Model family & quantization
- Candidate: open-70B family (we validated a 70B/34B family during internal tests).
- Recommendation: 70B quantized to 4-bit (~8–10GB VRAM with optimized kernels) for Dedicated (pinned). 34B as a fallback variant for cost-sensitive routes.
- Streaming + KV cache: enable streaming responses with KV cache pinned to worker process memory; this saves ~25–40% on per-request token compute for repeated prefixes.

2) Latency/throughput targets (example on p5-equivalent nodes):
- Single-request (no batch): 32-token completion, 70B-4bit: p50 ~55ms, p95 ~120–140ms (depends on sequence lengths).
- Continuous batching (mixed workloads): with 8–12 concurrent batching window and autoscaling tuned for tail latency, effective p95 for interactive queries can be kept ~<160ms while improving throughput by 2x.
- Throughput estimate: 4 p5 nodes (16vA100 equiv) can sustain ~200–250 QPS steady for median workloads with batching; add burst pool for peak coverage.

3) Topology sketch (recommended staging → production path):
- Staging: Hosted API + traffic mirroring to a Dedicated small pool (2 nodes) for load tests.
- Prod: Dedicated pool in us-west-2 (pinned quantized model) behind an API gateway with routing policy: primary -> dedicated; fallback -> hosted quantized variant.
- DR/HA: cross-region read replica (us-east-1) with asynchronous model sync and circuit-breaker to fallback model.

4) Operational levers to reach your cost/latency goals
- Prefix/KV caching: TTL 30m; tune cache hit threshold for heavy search intents.
- Dynamic batching policy: max window 20ms for interactive routes; tune per-route.
- Quantization profiles: create two profiles (quality-first = 4-bit FP hybrid, cost-first = 8-bit int) and A/B traffic for validation.

5) Security & compliance notes for Private
- KMS/HSM for keys, centralized audit logs forwarded to your SIEM, and network peering with customer-managed ingress.
- We provide SOC2 artifacts and can add custom retention policies for logs in Private deployments.

Attachments included: redwood_deploy_sketch.pdf (sketches + rough node counts).

Open questions for you (so we can finalize numbers):
- Typical average response token count over a session (helps sizing).
- Acceptable p95 ceiling during peak (is 200ms permissible for short windows?).
- Preferred procurement timing for Dedicated reserve (monthly vs quarterly).

If it helps, I can prepare a 1-page tech decision matrix for the call Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

- p95 during short peak windows: we can tolerate up to 250ms for <5% of requests during flash events, but prefer p95 <= 150ms normally.
- Procurement: likely quarterly reserved capacity to start. Finance asked that we also see a 6-month spend projection for Dedicated vs Hosted.
